column1: # One note per line: id, points, text, then key=value fields, split by tabs. Format: https://teoyujie.org/api/notes.txt

column3: Size an air purifier by its CADR and your room
column5: why=For a typical 10–12 m² HDB bedroom, NEA suggests smoke CADR of about 130–156 m³/h or higher, depending on room size.

column3: Avoid air cleaners that intentionally generate ozone
column5: why=The US EPA advises against using air cleaners that intentionally generate ozone in occupied spaces.

column3: Check what a water filter is certified to remove
column5: why=Filters remove different substances. The CDC says to check the specific product certification and choose for the substance of concern.

column3: Compare washing machines on the water-efficiency label
column5: why=PUB labels household washing machines with two, three or four ticks for water efficiency.

column3: Check an N95 respirator against the NIOSH equipment list
column5: why=NIOSH says approved respirators have a printed TC approval number and recommends checking its certified equipment list.

column3: Choose UV400 or 100% UV protection on sunglasses
column5: why=The US FDA says sunglasses with either label block more than 99% of UVA and UVB radiation.

column3: Check sunscreen water resistance for swimming or sweating
column5: why=The American Academy of Dermatology says water-resistance labels indicate either 40 or 80 minutes in water; reapply as directed.

column3: Choose a smoke alarm with a 10-year built-in battery
column5: why=SCDF recommends home fire alarms with a built-in battery lasting 10 years, and says smoke detection provides earlier warning than heat detection.

column3: Check a fire extinguisher for its certification serial label
column5: why=SCDF says buyers can look for a serial label issued by a recognised certification body, physical damage and an operative pressure gauge.

column3: Compare appliance purchase price plus lifetime electricity cost
column5: why=NEA recommends adding purchase price to estimated annual energy cost multiplied by the appliance lifespan.

column3: Size your air conditioner for the floor area
column5: why=NEA says an oversized or undersized air conditioner operates less efficiently and gives a floor-area rule of thumb.

column3: Be wary of cosmetics promising miraculous results
column5: why=HSA says claims of quick, miraculous results may be uncertain and online reviews may not be from genuine consumers.

column3: Check air purifier filter replacement costs before buying
column5: why=The US EPA recommends considering both replacement filters and the cost of running a portable air cleaner.

column3: Check a toy's age label and small-parts warnings
column5: why=Singapore’s Consumer Product Safety Office advises choosing age-appropriate toys and following the labels; older children’s toys should be kept from younger ones.

column3: Check that a toy's button-battery compartment is secure
column5: why=Singapore’s Consumer Product Safety Office warns that swallowed button batteries can cause serious internal injuries or death.

column3: Check disinfectant concentration and contact time
column5: why=NEA says pathogens differ in resistance and the effective concentration and contact time depend on the disinfectant and pathogen.

column3: Choose the manufacturer-recommended PMD or e-bike charger
column5: why=SCDF advises using a power adaptor bearing the Safety Mark and recommended by the device manufacturer.

column3: Compare similar foods using the per-100 g nutrition column
column5: why=HealthHub says nutrition panels show amounts per 100 g or 100 ml as well as per serving, allowing objective comparisons.

column3: Check the nutrition panel behind a reduced-fat claim
column5: why=HealthHub notes that reduced fat does not necessarily mean low fat; the panel shows actual nutrient amounts.

column3: Check the assumptions behind an appliance energy-cost label
column5: why=NEA’s air-conditioner annual cost example uses S$0.27 per kWh and eight hours of daily use; your usage and tariff may differ.

column3: Search for product recalls before buying an appliance
column5: why=Singapore’s Consumer Product Safety Office advises an online search for recalls or safety flags before buying.

column3: Look for the NEA registration mark on mosquito repellent
column5: why=NEA says registered repellents display its logo and registration number and are assessed for safety and efficacy. Botanical repellents are exempt from registration.

column3: Be cautious of supplements promising rapid results
column5: why=HSA warns that supplements claiming rapid effects may contain undeclared potent medicinal ingredients.

column3: Compare health policies on exclusions and out-of-pocket costs
column5: why=MoneySense recommends checking exclusions, deductibles, co-insurance, benefit limits and waiting periods before buying health insurance.

column3: Check how health insurance premiums and renewal can change
column5: why=MoneySense advises asking whether premiums can change yearly, whether renewal is automatic and how a claim affects future premiums.

column3: Check existing coverage before buying more health insurance
column5: why=MoneySense suggests checking existing policies and employer coverage, including what happens to work benefits if you leave your job.

column3: Check pre-existing-condition cover before switching an IP
column5: why=MoneySense warns that conditions covered under a previous Integrated Shield Plan may lose coverage when switching to another plan.

column3: Compare life insurance features as well as premiums
column5: why=MoneySense says compareFIRST allows comparisons of insurance premiums, features, benefits and cash values across insurers.

column3: Ask what happens to a term policy premium on renewal
column5: why=MoneySense says renewal premiums may be revised according to age and are often not guaranteed.

column3: Check the surrender value before buying whole life insurance
column5: why=MoneySense describes whole life insurance as a long-term commitment and says early termination causes a loss.

column3: Check the free-look period and refund terms on a policy
column5: why=MoneySense says most policies have at least 14 days from receipt; travel, car and maid insurance are exceptions, and deductions can apply.

column3: Check a course’s ratings and participant count
column5: why=MySkillsFuture says its course pages show survey-based quality and outcomes indicators and the number of course attendees.

column3: Check whether a course accepts Mid-Career Credit
column5: why=MySkillsFuture says Mid-Career Credit applies only to selected courses, identified on the course directory and detail page.

column3: Confirm preschool vacancies directly with the centre
column5: why=LifeSG says vacancies change with ongoing enrolments and recommends contacting shortlisted centres to confirm availability.

column3: Read a stay’s cancellation and refund policy before paying
column5: why=The US FTC recommends obtaining the cancellation and refund terms before paying for travel or a vacation rental.

column3: Check the final travel total and preselected add-ons
column5: why=The US FTC advises reviewing preselected options and comparing the final checkout total with the original price.

column3: Verify a Singapore travel agent in STB’s directory
column5: why=STB advises checking the travel agent’s licence in its TRUST directory before transacting.

column3: Try shoes with the socks you intend to wear
column5: why=Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS advises trying shoes with your usual socks or tights and not relying on breaking in an uncomfortable fit.

column3: Try shoes late in the day if your feet swell
column5: why=Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS recommends shopping at the end of the day when feet that tend to swell may be largest.

column3: Visit a preschool and ask about its teacher-child ratio
column5: why=Singapore Global Network’s education guide suggests visiting teachers and asking about the ratio and how they update parents.

column3: Compare preschool hours with your family’s schedule
column5: why=Singapore Global Network notes that preschool timetables vary, with some offering half or full days and others longer care hours.

column3: Ask for an itemised renovation quote and work schedule
column5: why=CCCS recommends itemised pricing, a detailed scope and agreed start and completion dates in renovation contracts.

column3: Agree renovation changes and their costs in writing
column5: why=CaseTrust says accredited renovation businesses must agree variations in writing before work begins and communicate additional costs.

column3: Check how a renovation deposit is protected
column5: why=CaseTrust says accredited renovation businesses must purchase a deposit performance bond and provide proof of prepayment protection.

column3: Ask for renovation payments tied to completed milestones
column5: why=CASE advises negotiating a low deposit and progressive payments as each stage is completed rather than paying a large sum upfront.

column3: Photograph renovation defects before the final payment
column5: why=CASE recommends photographing outstanding defects and ensuring they are rectified before paying in full.

column3: Check the renovation workmanship warranty and its terms
column5: why=CaseTrust requires accredited renovation businesses to provide a 12-month workmanship warranty, subject to contract terms.

column3: Negotiate furniture payment after satisfactory delivery
column5: why=CASE recommends negotiating a small deposit and paying the balance after furniture is delivered in satisfactory condition.

column3: Inspect a shared car and report defects before driving
column5: why=CASE recommends using the operator’s checklist, reporting defects immediately and not driving when there are issues.

column3: Compare car-sharing excess, insurance and cancellation terms
column5: why=The CaseTrust-LTA scheme calls for clear liability rules, including excess payable, and disclosure of prices and surcharges.

column3: Ask a repair shop for a written estimate of parts and labour
column5: why=The US FTC recommends a written estimate identifying the fault, required parts and expected labour charge.

column3: Compare a workshop's service schedule with your car manual
column5: why=The US FTC notes some shops recommend more frequent maintenance than manufacturers and advises asking why.

column3: Ask what a car repair warranty covers and get it in writing
column5: why=The US FTC notes repair warranties can have limits on time, mileage and authorised repairers; there is no standard warranty.

column3: Compare broadband costs over the full contract term
column5: why=UK regulator Ofcom recommends adding setup fees to monthly charges and checking the full term and any price rises.

column3: Check the broadband contract's exit and notice terms
column5: why=CASE advises scrutinising termination clauses and has noted that notice periods differ among Singapore providers.

column3: Get beauty package services, prices and expiry in writing
column5: why=CASE advises asking for written details of the services, pricing and validity before committing to a beauty package.

column3: Check a beauty package's cooling-off terms before paying
column5: why=CASE says CaseTrust-accredited beauty, spa and wellness businesses offer a five-day cooling-off period for unutilised services.

column3: Buy ready-to-eat raw fish only from licensed establishments
column5: why=SFA advises confirming the fish is intended for raw consumption; raw fish carries foodborne illness risk even with precautions.

column3: Check SFA approval before buying raw fish from a food stall
column5: why=SFA maintains records of food stalls and caterers approved to sell ready-to-eat raw fish dishes; restaurants operate under different rules.

column3: Check an imported appliance's voltage and plug before buying
column5: why=CPSO says Singapore's electricity supply is 230 V at 50 Hz and advises checking the appliance's rated voltage and plug for local use.

column3: Verify a controlled appliance's SAFETY Mark in CPSO's register
column5: why=CPSO recommends searching the registration number or model and checking that the registered product details match the appliance.

column3: Check a rechargeable appliance's local after-sales support
column5: why=CPSO recommends sellers with locally available customer service and warranty services for lithium-ion devices.

column3: Consider whether you need a fridge's ice and water dispensers
column5: why=NEA says automatic icemakers and through-the-door dispensers increase a refrigerator's energy use.

column3: Look for a dryer moisture sensor that stops a finished load
column5: why=NEA recommends energy-saving features such as a moisture sensor that turns off the dryer when clothes are dry.

column3: Check a tap or shower fitting for its WELS label
column5: why=PUB advises checking water fittings for WELS labels and provides a list of registered products and suppliers.

column3: Compare light bulbs by lumens for the brightness you want
column5: why=The US EPA's bulb guide recommends focusing on lumen output when matching a replacement bulb's light output.

column3: Check a bulb is dimmable if your fixture has a dimmer
column5: why=The US EPA's bulb guide recommends a bulb marked dimmable for a dimmer and checking control compatibility with the manufacturer.

column3: Use Kelvin to choose a bulb's warmer or cooler appearance
column5: why=The US EPA guide says lower Kelvin numbers look more yellowish while higher numbers look whiter or bluer.

column3: Question antibacterial claims on bamboo-derived rayon
column5: why=The US FTC says there is no evidence that rayon made from processed bamboo is naturally antibacterial.

column3: Check a baby bouncer's restraints and folding lock
column5: why=CPSO recommends a durable restraint and a lock to prevent an accidental fold, as well as checking for pinch gaps and detachable small parts.

column3: Fit a child car seat to both your child and your car
column5: why=The American Academy of Pediatrics says a suitable seat fits the child's size and vehicle and can be installed and used correctly.

column3: Avoid a second-hand child car seat with unknown history
column5: why=The American Academy of Pediatrics advises against used seats of unknown history and seats involved in moderate or severe crashes.

column3: Check a used child seat's model and manufacture date
column5: why=The American Academy of Pediatrics says these details are needed to check recalls and recommends checking the maker's usable life.

column3: Check children's toys for loose or detachable magnets
column5: why=CPSO warns of severe injury if strong magnets are swallowed and recommends inspecting toys for detachable magnetic parts.

column3: Compare the drained weight of food packed in brine
column5: why=SFA's labelling guide says foods such as tuna or chickpeas packed in brine declare both net and drained weights.

column3: Compare glazed frozen food by net weight, not gross weight
column5: why=SFA's labelling guide says the net weight of ice-glazed frozen food excludes the weight of the ice glaze.

column3: Check sugar on the panel even if the pack says no added sugar
column5: why=HealthHub notes that no added sugar does not necessarily mean no sugar and advises reading the nutrition information panel.

column3: Match pet food's life-stage claim to your dog or cat
column5: why=WSAVA says nutritional profiles differ for growth, reproduction and adult maintenance; all-life-stages diets are formulated for growth and reproduction.

column3: Do not judge pet food quality by "premium" or "holistic" alone
column5: why=WSAVA says marketing terms such as premium and holistic have little practical value for nutritional assessment.

column3: Ask pet food makers who formulates the diet
column5: why=WSAVA recommends asking about the formulator's experience and qualifications as well as the company's nutrition expertise.

column3: Ask pet food makers how they test the finished product
column5: why=WSAVA recommends asking about ingredient checks, finished-diet nutrient analysis and safety testing as part of quality control.

column3: Ask for a pet food's calories if the label does not show them
column5: why=WSAVA says calorie information helps prevent unintentional overfeeding and can be requested from the manufacturer if absent from the label.

column3: Choose a child's bike for their current size, not to grow into
column5: why=CPSO recommends a bicycle of the right size that gives good balance, not one a child has outgrown or that is too big.

column3: Check a child's cycling helmet fits before buying
column5: why=CPSO says a helmet must fit well for proper protection and notes that children can outgrow theirs.

column3: Avoid UVC sterilising devices for home disinfection
column5: why=NEA advises households not to use UVC disinfection sterilisers: unintended exposure can injure eyes and skin.

column3: Check an LED bulb is rated for an enclosed fixture
column5: why=The US Department of Energy says enclosed fixtures trap heat, which can affect LED performance and life; check the package or specifications.

column3: Check a bulb's colour rendering where accurate colour matters
column5: why=The US Department of Energy says colour rendering index measures how a light renders colours relative to a reference on a 0–100 scale.

column3: Check a repellent's protection time and reapplication directions
column5: why=CDC says duration varies by formulation, activity and exposure; higher active-ingredient concentrations generally last longer, with exceptions.

column3: Ask a dentist about toothpaste for a child under three
column5: why=HealthHub notes fluorosis concerns and recommends consulting a dentist about use of 1,000 ppm fluoride toothpaste in children under three.

column3: Check the infant formula stage against your baby's age
column5: why=HealthHub says stage 2 formula is for 6–12 months and should not be given to infants aged 0–6 months.

column3: Seek medical advice before choosing specialised infant formula
column5: why=HealthHub says specialised formulas are for specific medical conditions and advises parents to seek medical advice before using them.

column3: Check a licensed stall's current SAFE grade online
column5: why=SFA says diners can scan the QR code on the licence or use its track-records page; old physical grade decals may be outdated.

column3: Read what a food stall's SAFE grade measures
column5: why=SFA says SAFE grades use food-safety track records over time; establishments operating for less than a year start with a NEW grade.

column3: Ask for sauce or gravy on the side when limiting sodium
column5: why=HealthHub says sauces, gravy and soups often contain high sodium and suggests requesting less or having sauce on the side.

column3: Look for the lower-sodium dining identifier on a dish
column5: why=HealthHub says participating outlets offer dishes prepared with lower-sodium salt, sauces and seasonings.

column3: Add vegetables to a hawker meal that has little produce
column5: why=HealthHub suggests a side of greens with chicken rice or extra vegetables with noodles, using My Healthy Plate as a guide.

column3: Ask whether brown rice is available at the stall
column5: why=HealthHub suggests asking about brown rice or looking for the wholegrain-options identifier when eating out.

column3: Do not assume a home food seller needs an SFA licence
column5: why=SFA says small home-based food businesses do not need its licence but still must comply with food-safety requirements.

column3: Check a plumber's PUB licence for regulated plumbing work
column5: why=PUB says regulated water-service and sanitary work requires a licensed plumber, while listed simple tasks may be done by handymen.

column3: Verify the worker's EMA licence before home rewiring
column5: why=EMA says new wiring, rewiring and extensions require a licensed worker; changing a bulb does not unless wiring work is involved.

column3: Use a licensed worker to install a piped-gas appliance
column5: why=EMA says piped-gas appliances require licensed installation and a written statement that the appliance was tested and is safe to use.

column3: Verify a vector-control company's NEA licence before hiring
column5: why=NEA advises checking the operator's licence and the credentials of personnel handling pesticides for mosquito or cockroach treatment.

column3: Ask pest-control firms for methods and a written work scope
column5: why=NEA suggests checking experience and methods in quotes, specifying the work scope and requesting reports of inspections and treatments.

column3: Look for anti-tip hardware when buying tall furniture
column5: why=CPSO recommends securing bookcases and dressers using anti-tip wall brackets, braces or straps to reduce tip-over injuries.

column3: Ask how a prepaid fitness package is protected
column5: why=CaseTrust says qualifying accredited fitness centres protect advance fees, but fees worth less than two months of service are exempt.

column3: Consider pay-per-use before committing to a long gym package
column5: why=CASE notes that a large prepayment can be lost if the business closes and suggests considering pay-per-use or smaller commitments.

column3: Check critical-illness definitions and waiting periods
column5: why=MoneySense says payout depends on the policy's illness definitions and that waiting periods can apply for certain illnesses or surgery.

column3: Check whether a travel seller needs a Singapore licence
column5: why=STB says its licensing rules have exceptions, including some overseas transactions and certain local walking tours.

column3: Turn a garment inside out and inspect its seams
column5: why=University of Georgia Extension recommends checking for puckered or fraying seams and properly finished raw edges.

column3: Check stitching at pockets and other garment stress points
column5: why=University of Kentucky Extension recommends secure, even stitching with reinforced stress points such as pockets.

column3: Test the zip and buttons before buying clothes
column5: why=Kansas State University Extension advises checking that zippers operate and are securely sewn and buttons fit their holes.

column3: Sit, walk and bend when trying on a garment
column5: why=Kansas State University Extension recommends moving in a garment to check fit, including whether it needs pulling or tugging after movement.

column3: Check the care label and dry-cleaning cost before buying
column5: why=University of California Extension advises reading ready-to-wear care labels and considering the added expense of dry cleaning.

column3: Inspect used clothes at knees, elbows and other stress points
column5: why=University of California Extension recommends checking worn areas, stitching, elastic, zips, buttonholes and buttons on used clothing.

column3: Fit shoes to the larger foot if your feet differ in size
column5: why=The American Podiatric Medical Association notes feet can differ in size and recommends fitting to the larger foot.

column3: Leave room for a child's toes when fitting shoes
column5: why=The American Podiatric Medical Association suggests about 10–15 mm in front of the longest toe and enough width at the widest part of the foot.

column3: Check cosmetics for ingredients you know you react to
column5: why=HSA advises reading the ingredient list and notes that even hypoallergenic products can cause allergic reactions.

column3: Do not assume natural cosmetics are necessarily safer
column5: why=HSA says natural or organic products are not necessarily safer: some plant ingredients can cause allergies.

column3: Check a cosmetic has an ingredient list and local contact
column5: why=HSA says cosmetic labels must include ingredients, a batch number and the Singapore name and address of the responsible company.

column3: Check what a supplement quality seal actually covers
column5: why=The US NIH says independent quality seals can indicate testing of contents and contaminants but do not guarantee safety or effectiveness.

column3: Do not treat "standardised" as proof of supplement quality
column5: why=The US NIH says the term on a supplement label does not necessarily indicate product quality.

column3: Compare a mobile plan with your actual monthly data usage
column5: why=UK regulator Ofcom suggests checking past usage in your provider's app or website before choosing an allowance.

column3: Check speed and fair-use limits on unlimited mobile plans
column5: why=Ofcom advises checking whether an unlimited plan has fair-use restrictions, speed limits or limits on use abroad.

column3: Check roaming allowances and charges for your destinations
column5: why=Ofcom suggests checking whether roaming is included or requires an add-on and what calls, messages and data will cost abroad.

column3: Compare handset bundles with a phone plus SIM-only plan
column5: why=Ofcom notes handset bundles can cost more over the contract than buying a phone separately; include upfront charges and extras.

column3: Check mobile coverage where you live, work and travel
column5: why=Ofcom recommends comparing network availability and performance in places where you need the connection.

column3: Check a router's Singapore cybersecurity label
column5: why=CSA says routers sold for local use must meet at least CLS Level 1 and display the CSA label and IMDA compliance label.

column3: Check the exact smart device in CSA's active product list
column5: why=CSA's Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme list shows active and archived product registrations, including model, level and expiry date.

column3: Compare what the cybersecurity label's levels actually test
column5: why=CSA says Level 3 includes third-party software analysis, while Level 4 adds structured third-party penetration testing.

column3: Choose headphones that fit well in your usual environment
column5: why=WHO says well-fitted, noise-cancelling headphones can reduce the need to raise volume in noisy settings; listening level and duration still matter.

column3: Check for sound-exposure monitoring on audio devices
column5: why=WHO recommends considering devices with safe-listening features such as volume limiting and exposure monitoring.

column3: Do not substitute ordinary noise-cancelling headphones for hearing protection
column5: why=US NIOSH says active-noise-cancelling headphones should not be considered hearing protection unless labelled with a noise-reduction rating.

column3: Check the real item photos when buying second-hand electronics
column5: why=The US FTC advises looking for pictures of the actual item rather than relying on stock photos when judging condition.

column3: Check the anti-dandruff ingredient on the exact bottle
column5: why=FairPrice lists piroctone olamine in Head & Shoulders 72h Oil Control 480 g, illustrating that the active can differ across variants.

column3: Choose food containers intended for repeated use
column5: why=SFA says takeaway plastic food containers are designed for one-time use and should not be reused for storing or reheating food.

column3: Plan for water-filter cleaning and replacement before buying
column5: why=PUB says filters can become breeding grounds for bacteria if they are not cleaned or replaced regularly.

column3: Use a food thermometer to check meat's internal temperature
column5: why=US food-safety guidance recommends a food thermometer in the thickest part, avoiding bone, fat and gristle.

column3: Use a fridge thermometer if your fridge lacks a display
column5: why=US CDC advises checking the refrigerator is at 40°F (about 4.4°C) or below; a separate appliance thermometer can help when no built-in thermometer is present.

column3: Check ingredient and advisory labels for your food allergen
column5: why=SFA advises checking ingredients and looking for warnings such as may contain when avoiding a food allergen.

column3: Ask the food maker if a cross-contact risk is unclear
column5: why=SFA advises contacting the food business if clarification is needed about potential allergens in prepacked food.

column3: Do not use brown colour alone to identify wholegrain bread
column5: why=HealthHub says bread or crackers may be brown because of added colouring, while some wholegrain foods are light in colour.

column3: Look for whole grains near the top of the ingredient list
column5: why=HealthHub suggests wholewheat or whole oats ideally appear first or second; an ingredient list alone does not state the wholegrain percentage.

column3: Do not assume high-fibre or multigrain means wholegrain
column5: why=HealthHub notes added bran can increase fibre without making a product wholegrain, and multigrain does not necessarily mean wholegrain.

column3: Buy shellfish from SFA-approved businesses, not the wild
column5: why=SFA warns that wild shellfish may contain marine biotoxins that cooking does not destroy.

column3: Avoid damaged packaging when buying nuts or nut butter
column5: why=SFA advises rejecting unclean, opened or damaged packages and keeping nuts cool and dry to reduce exposure to mycotoxins.

column3: Check whether raw shellfish is designated ready-to-eat
column5: why=SFA says raw shellfish carries risks; pregnant, young, older and immunocompromised people should avoid it even when labelled ready-to-eat.

column3: Check travel insurance limits and claim requirements
column5: why=STB's travel-insurance guide advises reading claim limits and the steps needed to claim before purchasing a policy.

column3: Check whether travel insurance covers your planned activities
column5: why=STB notes that some policies exclude or charge extra for higher-risk activities such as skiing.

column3: Check travel cover for pre-existing medical conditions
column5: why=STB says some policies may exclude pre-existing conditions or require an additional premium; check the policy before buying.

column3: Check travel insurance covers the full trip and travel days
column5: why=STB recommends considering the entire journey, including flights to and from the destination.

column3: Check travel-agent insolvency cover in your policy
column5: why=STB advises checking whether the policy covers insolvency of the particular travel agent from which the trip was bought.

column3: Check a flight fare's baggage, changes and refund rules
column5: why=The US Department of Transportation notes that fare types can differ in baggage allowances, seat assignment and refundability.

column3: Check which airline actually operates a code-share flight
column5: why=The US Department of Transportation explains that the airline selling a ticket may differ from the airline operating the flight.

column3: Check every airline's carry-on size and weight limits
column5: why=The US Department of Transportation advises checking each airline on a multi-airline itinerary because limits can differ.

column3: Search a vacation rental's address and operator before paying
column5: why=The US FTC warns of hijacked and fictitious listings and suggests checking the address and operator against other sources.

column3: Check whether you are booking directly or through an agent
column5: why=The US FTC notes that the seller can affect refund handling, travel points and the price of changes or cancellations.

column3: Verify a general-insurance agent's registration before buying
column5: why=MoneySense advises asking for the agent's GIA number and checking permission to sell with the Agents Registration Board.

column3: Check what data a smart device collects before buying
column5: why=Australia's cyber-security agency recommends checking what information a smart device collects and with whom it is shared.

column3: Check whether a smart device lets you change its password
column5: why=Australia's cyber-security agency lists changeable passwords and manufacturer security updates among things to check before buying.

column3: Reset a second-hand smart device before using it
column5: why=Australia's cyber-security agency recommends a factory reset so the previous owner no longer has access to the device or your data.

column3: Check what a printer's stated cartridge yield measures
column5: why=ISO/IEC 24711 measures colour ink-cartridge page yield on plain paper; the test does not establish print quality or reliability.

column3: Do not use office-page ink yield as a photo-print guarantee
column5: why=ISO says its colour yield test pages represent office and home documents and are not intended to represent photo printing.

column3: Check built-in protection before buying extra antivirus software
column5: why=Australia's cyber-security agency says most modern Microsoft and Apple computers include built-in antivirus and advises comparing added features and costs.

column3: Verify the registration of your optometrist or optician
column5: why=MOH recommends checking the attending practitioner's identity against the register; its Health Professionals Portal links to the search.

column3: Compare vacuum cleaning tests for your own floor type
column5: why=CHOICE tests stick vacuums separately for hard-floor dirt pickup, quick and thorough carpet cleaning, and pet hair removal.

column3: Check vacuum filter replacement and cleaning requirements
column5: why=CHOICE notes that HEPA filters need regular cleaning and eventual replacement; the interval depends on use and dust.

column3: Check whole-machine filtration, not just the vacuum filter
column5: why=CHOICE notes that a poor seal around a good filter can let some exhaust air bypass it.

column3: Test vacuum manoeuvrability rather than judging by wattage
column5: why=CHOICE says strong suction and high motor wattage do not necessarily mean better cleaning performance.

column3: Check an induction pan's base with a magnet
column5: why=CHOICE says the magnet should stick well to the base; aluminium pans can work if they have a suitable steel plate.

column3: Match pan size to your cooktop's cooking zone
column5: why=CHOICE recommends matching saucepan size to the element, especially on ceramic and induction cooktops.

column3: Try one induction pan before buying a whole set
column5: why=CHOICE notes that individual pans respond differently to an induction cooktop and suggests trying one basic pan first.

column3: Try a kitchen knife for grip and balance before buying
column5: why=CHOICE recommends testing knives for comfort and notes its tests did not find forged knives necessarily better than stamped ones.

column3: Try a mattress on a base like the one you use at home
column5: why=CHOICE notes that a soft mattress can feel different on fixed slats or a hard surface than on a showroom ensemble base.

column3: Match replacement tyres to the car's size, load and speed ratings
column5: why=Michelin Singapore notes that tyres with the same dimensions can have different load and speed ratings; check the vehicle specifications.

column3: Compare independent braking and handling tests for tyres
column5: why=Michelin notes that independent testers compare tyres on criteria including braking, handling, noise and rolling resistance.

column3: Check the vehicle manual before mixing tyres on a 4x4
column5: why=Michelin advises following the vehicle maker's tyre recommendations and checking before fitting tyres with different front-to-rear wear.

column3: Inspect used tyres for damage and ask about their history
column5: why=Bridgestone Singapore warns that used tyres may have unknown repairs or uneven wear that can affect safety.

column3: Check a child car seat against Singapore's approved standards
column5: why=Singapore Traffic Police added ECE R129 in 2025 and says some older British and Japanese standards cease to be approved from 1 January 2031.

column3: Check a power bank's watt-hours before buying it for flights
column5: why=CAAS permits up to 100 Wh; above 100 Wh and up to 160 Wh needs airline approval, and above 160 Wh is not allowed. Airlines may be stricter.

column3: Match fast charging across the power bank, cable and device
column5: why=CHOICE notes that all three must be compatible for fast charging; USB-C cables can have different capabilities.

column3: Check a USB-C cable's power rating and data rate separately
column5: why=USB-IF's compliance programme requires power markings and, except for USB 2.0 cables, a supported data-rate marking.

column3: Check product recalls and local service before buying electronics
column5: why=Singapore's CPSO recommends checking recalls and choosing sellers with locally available after-sales and warranty services.

column3: Observe how preschool educators interact with children
column5: why=ECDA advises watching interactions and asking about the training and experience of staff who will care for your child.

column3: Ask a preschool how it handles your child's food allergies
column5: why=ECDA advises discussing dietary restrictions and allergies with the preschool to ensure the child's needs are addressed.

column3: Ask a preschool about its emergency arrangements
column5: why=ECDA recommends finding out how the preschool typically responds to emergencies.

column3: Compare preschool extras as well as the programme fee
column5: why=ECDA suggests checking transport, materials, learning journeys and other miscellaneous costs when assessing a preschool budget.

column3: Check a preschool's curriculum against your child's needs
column5: why=ECDA notes that preschools use different education philosophies and curriculum approaches, and recommends considering their fit with the child.

column3: Ask employers whether a course's credential is useful
column5: why=The US FTC suggests asking employers what training and experience they value, and comparing what qualification each programme awards.

column3: Inspect the equipment and instructor credentials on a practical course
column5: why=The US FTC suggests visiting facilities, asking whether equipment matches industry use, and checking instructor qualifications.

column3: Review a private course's total fees and withdrawal terms in writing
column5: why=A SkillsFuture student advisory recommends checking all fees, payment dates and refund terms in the completed contract before signing.

column3: Check what fee protection a private course actually provides
column5: why=A SkillsFuture student advisory recommends reviewing the fee protection scheme and its coverage in the contract before signing.

column3: Verify a promised course attachment with the host organisation
column5: why=A SkillsFuture guide suggests confirming the organisation, attachment period and alternative if the placement becomes unavailable.

column3: Treat coaching testimonials and guaranteed income claims cautiously
column5: why=The US FTC warns that testimonials can be misleading and that claims of guaranteed high earnings with little risk indicate a scam.

column3: Compare Nutri-Grade within the same drink category
column5: why=HealthHub says the grade measures sugar and saturated fat, not every nutrient; for example, milk also provides protein and calcium.

column3: Consider unsweetened frozen produce when fresh is unavailable
column5: why=HealthHub says frozen fruits and vegetables can be as nutritious as fresh produce and are a convenient alternative.

column3: Do not assume organic produce is automatically more nutritious
column5: why=HealthHub says studies have not reached a clear conclusion that organic produce is healthier, safer or tastier than conventional produce.

column3: Check mango ripeness by feel and fragrance
column5: why=HealthHub describes ripe mangoes as slightly soft and usually intensely fragrant.

column3: Check wholegrain percentages rather than inferring them from fibre
column5: why=HealthHub says an ingredient list and nutrition panel do not tell you the wholegrain amount, and high fibre alone does not mean wholegrain.

column3: Check with a clinician before potassium salt if kidney function is impaired
column5: why=HealthHub advises people with conditions that impair potassium excretion, such as late-stage chronic kidney disease, to consult a healthcare professional.

column3: Check whether a laptop's RAM and storage can be upgraded
column5: why=CHOICE notes that some laptops have soldered memory or inaccessible storage, so upgrades may be difficult or impossible.

column3: Check required school software works on the laptop before buying
column5: why=CHOICE notes that some specialised applications are exclusive to one operating system and recommends checking required software compatibility.

column3: Compare laptop battery tests as well as advertised runtime
column5: why=CHOICE found school-appropriate laptops typically lasted less in its tests than their advertised battery life.

column3: Measure the viewing distance before choosing a TV size
column5: why=CHOICE recommends measuring from the seated viewer's eyes to the screen, rather than using the full wall-to-wall room length.

column3: Check a TV's picture from the sides and in normal mode
column5: why=CHOICE notes that colour and contrast can fall off at an angle and shop displays may use unusually bright, saturated settings.

column3: Match a streaming device's HDR formats to your TV
column5: why=CHOICE notes that HDR10+ and Dolby Vision are not available on every streaming device; the TV and device must support matching formats.

column3: Check an SD card's format against your device before buying
column5: why=The SD Association says an SDHC-only host cannot use SDXC or SDUC cards; consult the device manual for supported formats.

column3: Match a recording card's speed class to the camera requirement
column5: why=The SD Association explains that speed classes specify minimum sequential performance under defined conditions, important for continuous video recording.

column3: Ask how long a smart device will receive software updates
column5: why=The US FTC recommends checking the manufacturer's stated update period and considering how the device will work after updates stop.

column3: Weigh a typical laundry load before choosing washer capacity
column5: why=CHOICE suggests weighing yourself with and without the laundry basket to estimate a typical load, while allowing for bulky items such as bedding.

column3: Measure the washer space with its door or lid open
column5: why=CHOICE recommends checking clearance for loading, the laundry basket, doors and access to power and water connections.

column3: Compare a washer's actual cycle time, not just its quick wash
column5: why=CHOICE found some front-loader cycles take hours and notes quick cycles may not suit large or heavily soiled loads.

column3: Check washer spin-speed choices for your clothes and drying method
column5: why=CHOICE notes faster spins extract more water for shorter drying, while lower speeds can suit delicates or reduce creasing.

column3: Check washer-dryer combo drying time and water use
column5: why=CHOICE notes that some combination machines take a long time to dry and some use water during the drying stage.

column3: Compare detergent tests using your machine type and usual stains
column5: why=CHOICE tests detergents in front and top loaders using a cold wash and scores several stains, including sweat, grass and cooking oil.

column3: Check whether detergent pods suit your usual load size
column5: why=CHOICE notes that individual pods are convenient but their dose is not as easily adjusted as loose powder or liquid.

column3: Check stain-remover tests against detergent alone
column5: why=CHOICE tests stain removers against detergent and water controls; some sprays in its test performed little better than no stain remover.

column3: Check a rice cooker's minimum as well as maximum batch size
column5: why=CHOICE says capacity usually counts cups of uncooked rice, while minimum batches may be around two supplied cups or more for larger models.

column3: Check how a rice cooker's lid and steam vent come apart for cleaning
column5: why=CHOICE notes sealed lids can have removable inner lids or vents, but the outer lid and steam vent also need cleaning.

column3: Compare rice cookers on the type of rice you actually cook
column5: why=CHOICE tests white and brown rice separately and notes that brown rice can take substantially longer than white rice.

column3: Listen to a fan at the speed you would use for sleeping
column5: why=CHOICE notes that fan noise varies by setting and a whine or buffeting sound can be more distracting than steady noise.

column3: Compare pedestal and tower fans for airflow and floor space
column5: why=In CHOICE tests pedestal fans generally delivered stronger airflow, while tower fans occupied less floor space.

column3: Measure the room before choosing a ceiling fan
column5: why=CHOICE recommends comparing room dimensions and your preferred speed range with the maker's sizing guidance.

column3: Check if a ceiling fan can accept a light later
column5: why=CHOICE notes that some fans are sold in separate light and no-light versions and cannot have a light added later.

column3: Check a new pillow fits your pillowcase before buying
column5: why=CHOICE found that some tested pillows differed from their stated dimensions and suggests taking the pillowcase or its measurements to the shop.

column3: Choose tofu and vegetables instead of fried yong tau foo items
column5: why=HealthHub suggests choosing tofu and assorted vegetables instead of fried ingredients when selecting yong tau foo.

column3: Leave some soup when limiting sodium in a noodle dish
column5: why=HealthHub notes that soup-based dishes can contain substantial sodium and suggests not drinking all the broth.

column3: Ask for plain rice instead of flavoured rice if reducing fat
column5: why=HealthHub recommends plain rice over fried or flavoured rice as one way to reduce fat intake when eating out.

column3: Ask for less or no sugar in freshly prepared drinks
column5: why=HealthHub suggests requesting less or no sugar in drinks, or choosing plain water.

column3: Look for the lower-calorie identifier on a specific dish
column5: why=HealthHub says a dish with the lower-calorie option identifier provides less than 500 calories per serving.

column3: Look for separate handling of raw and ready-to-eat foods
column5: why=SFA advises checking that raw and cooked foods are displayed separately and handled with separate utensils and equipment.

column3: Check hot and cold buffet items are held at safe temperatures
column5: why=SFA advises hot buffet food be held above 60°C and cold food displayed on ice or in refrigerated cabinets below 5°C.

column3: Check the consume-by time when ordering catered food
column5: why=SFA advises checking the caterer's time stamp and consuming catered food within the stated consume-by time.

column3: Check toe-box width and depth, not just shoe length
column5: why=Guy's and St Thomas' NHS guidance recommends enough depth above the toes and a rounded or square front that does not squeeze them.

column3: Leave space in front of your longest toe when fitting shoes
column5: why=Guy's and St Thomas' NHS guidance suggests about 1 cm of space for walking because feet extend as you move.

column3: Do not count on uncomfortable shoes becoming comfortable later
column5: why=Bradford NHS guidance says a correctly fitting shoe should generally feel comfortable from the start without needing to be broken in.

column3: Try shoes with your prescribed insoles before buying
column5: why=The American Podiatric Medical Association recommends bringing prescribed orthotics to try in prospective shoes.

column3: Check that shoes fasten securely without squeezing the toes
column5: why=Guy's and St Thomas' NHS guidance says laces or hook-and-loop fastenings secure the shoe around the foot while leaving space for toes.

column3: Check children's shoe fit again as their feet grow
column5: why=The American Podiatric Medical Association recommends checking children's shoe sizing every four to six months because feet grow and brands vary.

column3: Check running-shoe return terms before wearing them outdoors
column5: why=CHOICE found return and warranty terms differ between sellers and recommends checking what is covered before use.

column3: Check the seller and product source before choosing cheap medicine
column5: why=HSA warns against selecting health products on price alone and advises avoiding unfamiliar sellers unable to substantiate their supply source.

column3: Check a Singapore pharmacy's licence in HSA's register
column5: why=HSA's Infosearch links to the retail pharmacy licence holders database as well as its register of therapeutic products.

column3: Be suspicious of prescription medicines sold without a prescription
column5: why=HSA advises caution when an online seller offers prescription medicine without requiring a prescription.

column3: Ask a pharmacist whether a medicine suits you before comparing prices
column5: why=HealthHub says pharmacy-only medicines require a pharmacist's assessment of suitability even when no doctor's prescription is needed.

column3: Ask about interactions before adding a supplement to medicines
column5: why=HSA warns that combining supplements with certain medicines can cause harm and recommends advice from a doctor or pharmacist when unsure.

column3: Check an e-bike is LTA-approved, sealed and registered before use
column5: why=LTA requires power-assisted bicycles used on public roads and cycling paths to be type-approved, sealed and registered with a number plate.

column3: Arrange registration transfer when buying a registered e-bike
column5: why=LTA says a retailer or seller must transfer the registration when a registered power-assisted bicycle is bought, including second-hand.

column3: Check an e-bike's route before buying it for a daily commute
column5: why=LTA permits power-assisted bicycles on roads and shared paths, but not on footpaths.

column3: Check an e-scooter is registered and transfer ownership on purchase
column5: why=LTA advises buyers to ensure e-scooters are registered and the ownership transfer completed; new retail e-scooters need registration inspection.

column3: Check a bicycle's size and handbrake for public-path use
column5: why=LTA's public-path rules for manual bicycles specify a maximum 20 kg weight, 70 cm width and at least one functioning handlebar handbrake.

column3: Check medical-need eligibility before buying a mobility scooter
column5: why=LTA says consumers should obtain a Certificate of Medical Need or be exempt before purchase; only registered mobility scooters may be sold.

column3: Check the roast date and buy coffee in batches you will use
column5: why=CHOICE recommends checking the roast date and buying smaller batches to help keep beans fresh.

column3: Consider whole beans if you can grind shortly before brewing
column5: why=The Specialty Coffee Association notes that grinding speeds the loss of carbon dioxide compared with whole beans, alongside faster freshness changes.

column3: Store opened coffee away from moisture and sunlight
column5: why=CHOICE recommends an airtight container away from sunlight and moisture, such as in a dark pantry.

column3: Check which capsules fit a coffee machine before buying it
column5: why=CHOICE notes that capsule systems differ in compatibility, limiting the coffees available for a given machine.

column3: Add capsule cost to the purchase price of a pod coffee machine
column5: why=CHOICE advises considering the ongoing cost of pods as well as the machine, since costs vary by system and usage.

column3: Check coffee-machine cleaning tasks before choosing automatic
column5: why=CHOICE notes that automatic machines still need regular cleaning of parts such as milk containers, pipes, drip trays and water tanks.

column3: Choose a grinder that can produce the grind your brewer needs
column5: why=CHOICE notes that French press uses a coarser grind than espresso and its expert recommends a consistent burr grinder for home coffee.
